ariaLabels: Simulated paths with the scaled geometric average cG between 88 and 102, plotted against the basis A minus cG, at strike 95. The strike separates cG from A on the paths inside two wedges that meet at the strike: above the axis, where the proxy is below the strike and the option is in the money, and below it, where the proxy is above the strike and the option is out of the money.

The continuous price lies in [6.508371733, 6.518868974], the interval (1.3); the price under absorbed Euler with step 1/768 lies in [6.507844281, 6.519014106]. Both contain the proxy value 6.513251661289 and exclude 6.52.

Magnified around the proxy value: the proxy value 6.513251661289, known to plus or minus 0.00021, and the simulated price, close to 6.51335, which exceeds the proxy value by 0.000102 with standard error 0.000004.

The bound on the cost of the kink per unit of strike in Black's model at 35 percent volatility, against the time before the first fixing from one day to 24 months, on logarithmic scales, for averaging windows of one month, one quarter and one year. Each curve falls with the square root of the lead time and lies close to its leading term. The one-month curve passes through the four crude oil options of Table 1, two orders of magnitude below one cent on a 70-dollar barrel; the one-year curve crosses that level.

Monthly crude oil calls one to twelve months ahead, in cents per barrel on a logarithmic scale. Proved bound: 0.0081, 0.0047, 0.0033 and 0.0023 cents. Classical first-order estimate: 2.6 cents at every lead time, 320 to 1,140 times larger. A quote step is one cent per barrel.

The cost of the kink per unit of strike across strikes from 55 to 190, on logarithmic scales, for the twelve-fixing Heston contract. The cost peaks near strike 77 and falls steeply above 140; the second-order term follows it closely; the smaller of the two bounds of Theorem 3.3 lies above both at every strike. Dashed rules mark the strikes 95 and 110 of the spread.
Show the width budget, the change at the finest step or the interval for the Euler gap
Change in width from h=1/768 to h=1/1536: cost of the kink −0.000307, projection −0.000008, frequency tail under Q +0.000383; width from 0.021667063872 to 0.021734290027.

Proved intervals for the Euler gap, the price under the scheme minus the continuous price. h=1/384: −0.014169989568 to 0.013839530031. h=1/768: −0.011024692273 to 0.010642371599. h=1/1536: −0.010967952032 to 0.010766337995.

Three sizes of Euler error against the number of Euler steps per year, on logarithmic scales. The bias of the proxy value halves with each halving of the step and follows the first-order line across the ladder of twelve steps. The proved bounds on the Euler gap of the option at 384, 768 and 1,536 steps lie between 0.010 and 0.015, well above the bias. The simulated changes in the cost of the kink at 192 to 1,536 steps lie near one millionth, well below it.

ariaLabels: The weight on a unit Riccati residual against the time to maturity at which the residual occurs, over a six-month horizon. Both weights are forward variance curves: the curve under the pricing measure rises from 0.0262 for a residual six months before maturity to about 0.040 for a residual at maturity, and the curve under the half-share measure lies below it, by about 0.003 at maturity.

Netting ratios against the frequency from 0 to 128 for three positions on the strike ladder, with the share of the leg-by-leg node charge in each band of four units of frequency. The call spread rises from near zero to near one at the top of the grid; the butterfly follows its square; the basket starts at one and oscillates below a quarter. Short bars at the right edge mark the Herfindahl levels 0.707, 0.612 and 0.289. Three quarters of the node charge lies between 64 and 96.

Joint bounds in index points: H0 1.398, H1 0.379, H2 0.367, H3 0.132, H4 0.115, Q0 1.208, Q1 0.351, Q2 0.233. Leg-by-leg bounds: H0 2.680, H1 0.476, H3 0.159, H4 0.138, Q0 1.545, Q1 0.408, Q2 0.252. The tolerance is a quarter point.

Complete bounds of the three-month spread in index points. Joint 0.233318843, below a quarter point; leg-by-leg 0.252393939, above it. Shared components: absolute centre 0.149775147, strip remainder 0.000026654, exact infinite tail 0.038055248. Node support: joint 0.045461793, leg-by-leg 0.064536890.

The set of possible errors of the 4400 call and the 4500 call from the node radii of the three-month certificate, a rounded convex body inside its dashed bounding box. Two parallel lines in the direction of the spread touch the body and the corner of the box: the body's support is 0.045461793 index points and the box's is 0.064536890.

Positions certified out of 28 against the tolerance in index points at roughness 0.52. At tolerances of 1/4, 1/2 and 1 point the joint bound certifies 2, 28, 28 positions and the leg-by-leg bound 0, 13, 28.

Positions certified out of 28 against the tolerance in index points at roughness 0.60. At tolerances of 1/4, 1/2 and 1 point the joint bound certifies 10, 28, 28 positions and the leg-by-leg bound 1, 22, 28.

Positions certified out of 28 against the tolerance in index points at roughness 0.90. At tolerances of 1/4, 1/2 and 1 point the joint bound certifies 20, 25, 28 positions and the leg-by-leg bound 13, 25, 27.
Choose the number of time cells

In index points from the quoted ask. The 4400 call: quoted band 1.30 points wide, from bid 91.10 to ask 92.40; the certified model price is at least 0.490 above the ask, with lower end 92.886 against an ask of 92.396. The 4500 call: quoted band 1.21 points wide, from 55.00 to 56.20; the certified model price is at least 0.067 above the ask.

metadata.title: Jiritsu Network: Asset-Verification Partnerships and Issuer Ranking | Theodore Ouyang
metadata.description: I built the data and ranking system behind Jiritsu's partnerships for its asset-verification and privacy-preserving computation services, as the sole dedicated contributor for new issuers. I reported to co-founder Asher Gottesman and ran core-team reviews with technical and financial guidance from Gene Itkis of MIT Lincoln Laboratory and Michael Lustig, former Senior Managing Director at BlackRock. I screened more than 18,000 token records down to six proposed pilot counterparties and delivered the partnership recommendations to the board.

metadata.description: China Construction Bank's internal framework assessed sustainability on more than 30 indicators, some of which carried overlapping information.
